questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select no substitution required

The banquet hall __is been renovate__ recently.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 
• The word 'recently' indicates that the action has been performed not long ago. In this case we use the **present perfect tense** which means an action that has just been performed in the past and has a link with the present.
 
• The option which is in the present perfect tense is **'has been renovated'.**
 
• So, only option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. who.**

We need to use the correct pronoun in the blank. Let us look at the usage of all the mentioned pronouns:

 
• Which is used in asking for information specifying one or more people or things from a definite set.
 
• Whom is used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• That is used to identify a specific person or thing observed or heard by the speaker.
 
• **Who** is used to introduce a clause giving further information about a person or people previously mentioned.

The most appropriate word is 'who' as it is used to refer to the young boy in the news.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. from.**

Let us look at the usage of the prepositions-

 
• At means 'present in a specific location or the time when an event takes place'.
 
• **From** means 'indicating the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts'.
 
• For means 'the time for which an action is performed'.
 
• To means 'indicating the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts'.

The most appropriate word is 'from' as it indicates that he returned from the jungle.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select no substitution required

More than 60% of India’s population __live under the poverty line.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"lives below the poverty line".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject **"India’s population" **is singular; therefore, the verb should also be singular.
 
• The original sentence uses **"live," **which is plural.
 
• The correct form should be **"lives."**
 
• The correct preposition to use when referring to the level at which people are considered poor is **"below" **the poverty line, not **"under."**
 
• The phrase **"below the poverty line" **is a standard expression used to describe the threshold below which individuals or families are considered to be living in poverty.
 
• The use of the singular verb **"lives" **along with the correct preposition **"below" **correctly matches the subject and appropriately conveys the intended meaning.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 "lives beside the poverty line" changes the meaning entirely, suggesting proximity rather than an economic condition.
 
 
• "Beside" means at the side of or next to.
 
 
 
• Option 2 "no substitution required" is incorrect because the original usage of "live under the poverty line" is not standard and the verb tense does not match the singular subject.
 
• Option 3 "live by the poverty line" also changes the meaning, suggesting living according to the poverty line rather than beneath it in economic terms.
 
 
• "By" can mean close to or according to, which does not fit the intended context.

questions.question: In a code language, if ‘LODGE’ is written as ‘122254725’, then how will ‘CARING’ be written in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40ecf7153f4f1af657cb262f936e9489bdbd87c2984620c6b7bb64742576bfc9.png] 

Vowels are A, E, I, and U.

Here, vowels are represented with their squares and Consonants with their actual position.

The pattern followed is,

For LODGE,

The place value of L is 12

The place value of O is 15, 15² = 225

The place value of D is 4

The place value of G is 7

The place value of E is 5, 5² = 25

So,

LODGE is written as 122254725

Similarly,

CARING is written as,

The place value of C is 3

The place value of A is 1, 1² = 1

The place value of R is 18

The place value of I is 9, 9² = 81

The place value of N is 14

The place value of G is 7

So,

CARING is written as 311881147

Hence, “311881147” is the correct answer.

questions.question: Among 45 students of a class, 26 attend Yoga class, 28 attend Gymnastic class and 5 students attend neither Yoga nor Gymnastic class. How many students attend both Yoga and Gymnastic classes?
questions.solution:
Drawing the Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d6ff303bc18507e90abe7909328144c8070b7b290a4caec03ffcaaf1e3041e2.png] 

According to the given information,

There are 45 students in the class and 26 attend Yoga class, 28 attend Gymnastic class and 5 students attend neither Yoga nor Gymnastic class.

Number of students who attend both yoga and gymnastics class = (26 + 28 + 5) – 45

= 59 – 45

= 14

Hence, “14” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

I. Some guavas are apples.

II. All grapes are oranges.

III. Some apples are grapes.

Conclusions:

I. Some apples are oranges.

II. No orange is guava.

III. Some oranges are guavas.

options.text: Conclusion I and either II or III follow
Only either conclusion I or III follow

questions.solution:
Drawing the Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd7ce0c5d4a28d798557e7fe468939ce89ab2a0aa306ef60359123edbfa5b051.png] 

Conclusion 1: Some apples are oranges → True (This is definitely true)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6400a0850f6c1b7b99e76c86174917e2212f7f9963ff4fa5a6306e314a7b0699.png] 

Conclusion 2: No orange is guava → False (Possible but not definite)

Conclusion 3: Some oranges are guavas → False (Possible but not definite)

But, Conclusion 2 and conclusion 3 form a complementary pair.

Hence, “Conclusion 1 and either conclusion 2 or conclusion3” follow.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by four conclusions in the options. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which conclusion logically follows from the statements.

Statements:

No hospital is clinic.

All clinics are houses.
questions.solution:
Drawing the Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e1c103ecc19702951fe0675b9e90494181b656291dd4ee145418bb206da514e.png] 

Conclusion 1: Some houses are not hospitals → True (This is definitely true)

Conclusion 2: All houses are hospitals → False (This is definitely false)

Conclusion 3: All houses are clinics → False (Possible but not definite)

Conclusion 4: No house is hospital → False (Possible, but is not definite)

Hence, “only conclusion 1” follow.

questions.question: At the rate of 8% the amount invested earns a simple interest of Rs. 240 after 3 years. If the rate of interest been 5% more, then how much more interest would it have earned?
questions.solution:
**Short Trick:**

SI on rate 8% = Rs. 240

SI on Rate 5% = [240/8] × 5 = Rs. 150

**Detailed Method:**

SI = 240, r = 8% and time = 3 years

As we know,

SI = P × r × t/100

⇒ 240 = (P × 8 × 3)/100

⇒ P = (240 × 100)/24

⇒ P = 1000

Again,

New rate = 8% + 5% = 13%

P = 1000, and time = 3 years

SI = (1000 × 13 × 3)/100

⇒ SI = 390

∴ The interest more than that of before = 390 – 240 = 150.

• **Either of whose parents were born in India**
 
• **Who has been ordinarily resident in India for not less than five years, became a citizen of India.**
 
 
 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955 **deals with matters relating to acquisition, determination, and termination of Indian citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.

questions.question: Hind Swaraj was written by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.**__

__
 
• **Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule is a book written by Mohandas K. Gandhi in 1909.**__
 
• Expresses his views on Swaraj, modern civilization, mechanization, etc.
 
• The book was banned in 1910 by the British government in India as a seditious text.
 
• Gandhi's Hind Swaraj takes the form of a dialogue between two characters, "The Reader and The Editor".

questions.question: Which of the following is the instrument used in submarines to view objects above sea level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e., __**P**____eriscope__.

__
 
• A** periscope__**__ __consists of a series of mirrors used to observe objects at an offset distance from the eye.
 
• It is used in submarines to view objects above sea level.
 
• An **odometer **is used to measure the distance traveled by objects using revolutions per minute.
 
• A** pyrheliometer** is an instrument for the measurement of direct beam solar irradiance.
 
• A** hypsometer** is an instrument for measuring height or elevation.
